raw_response:
I will keep the land in the wheat-maize rotation. That is what I know best, it fits Quzhou County, and it gives me grain in both halves of the year without taking on too much risk. I would not split too much land into unfamiliar cash crops because I want steady output, simple field work, and something I can manage with my own experience. For the winter side, I will carry the winter wheat through with topdressing, irrigation, and disease control when needed, then harvest it in early summer. Right after that, I will put the same land into summer maize, using improved seed, keeping plant population even, applying fertilizer mainly around the key growth stages, and irrigating when the field is dry. I will keep pesticide use limited to what is necessary because that saves money and avoids waste. I will use ordinary tillage where it helps the wheat, and fast no-tillage sowing for maize after wheat because the time window is short and I do not want to lose soil moisture.
